video_title: Rasheed Wallace tells Mad Max what Portland is REALLY like

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on his rookie year adjustment and playing behind veterans
quotes.excerpt: I'm glad that he put the knowledge in me that, yo, you ain't going nowhere and be the man right away.

text_blocks.speaker: Vernon Maxwell
text_blocks.text: Tell me about the adjustments your rookie year and all that stuff, man. How that was for you your rookie year coming in the NBA?

text_blocks.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
text_blocks.text: I'm glad that going back to Bill E. Laimbeer, I'm glad that he put the knowledge in me that, yo, you ain't going nowhere and be the man right away. He was like, you were pretty good somewhat as a freshman, but you were coming off the bench behind Harry. Same thing when I got to Carolina, I'm coming off the bench behind the captain Eric Montross, my guy. Get to the league, all right, ain't nothing different. I'm coming off the bench behind C. Webb and George McCloud.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on the talent of his rookie Washington Bullets squad
quotes.excerpt: I'm like, man, we got a great team here, drafted by the Washington Bullets.
quotes.quote: I'm like, man, we got a great team here, drafted by the Washington Bullets. Jimmy Lynam was the coach. That team, we had Brent Price, Mark Price, Chris Whitney, and Robert Pack was my guards. My twos was Ledell Eackles, Calbert Cheaney, and Mitchell Butler. That's my guy too, and Don MacLean. Then the threes was, oh, and Tim Legler, I'm sorry, Tim Legler too, because he won the three-point contest that year, my rookie year. And then we had Juwan, of course, Chris, Big George, Bob McCann. I feel like I'm missing one person. I think that might have been it, but we had a nice little squad.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on his first NBA start and injury in Phoenix
quotes.excerpt: He had shot a ball and it hit off the rim and was bouncing into the seats.
quotes.quote: He had shot a ball and it hit off the rim and was bouncing into the seats. So you know how in Phoenix, that edge of that court, it's just a drop-off. So he's going after the ball and wham, his ankle up on that drop-off. And he came back limping and we all were like, uh-oh. And then he couldn't play that game. So you know, I'm thinking he all right anyway, because he still had his uni on. We going to team meeting, coach Lynam writing on the board, do this, do that. I'm paying attention, but I'm like, all right, I know C. Webb in there.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on his trade from Washington to Portland
quotes.excerpt: Got traded to Portland for Rod Strickland because I guess the Bullets didn't like their guards.
quotes.quote: Got traded to Portland for Rod Strickland because I guess the Bullets didn't like their guards. Mark Price retired. They ended up trading Brent Price. They got rid of all their guards pretty much, except Chris Whitney. They had Rod and Chris Whitney. Yeah, it was a big culture shock because now you're going to a predominantly white town, and everything that you were used to before, they ain't doing that out here. The music is different, everything is different.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on Portland as a family-friendly city
quotes.excerpt: Portland is a great city for family.
quotes.quote: Portland is a great city for family. If you're starting your family or you have a family already, more adolescent kids going into the teenage year, Portland is a great city. They got so much to do for kids, museums, they got a museum called OMSI. Museum for kids, they got a whole lot of stuff downtown. They right there on many different rivers, and you got the beach, you got the mountains, and you got the sand, the dunes. So Portland has all four climates, and it's like, man, you can do it. If your kids are sitting at home being like, I'm bored, well then damn, you ain't checked outside or something like, yo. But Portland was a great city though, made some lifelong friends out there.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on his favorite steak and eggs spot in Portland
quotes.excerpt: The restaurant is called Cafe Du Berry. World's best steak and eggs, bro.
quotes.quote: The restaurant is called Cafe Du Berry. World's best steak and eggs, bro. When I was playing in the league, I would put a contract on that. I'm telling you, this was fire. Aaron McKie and Gary Trent introduced me to this restaurant. So they was like, man, this joint good as steak and eggs, but I'm like, all right, whatever, like, this steak and eggs, it ain't that wonderful. That was stupendous. Okay, but oh bro, but the one downfall to it, it's like a little sauce that they put on top of the steak. That's the one downfall. The sauce is immaculate, but about a half hour, 40 minutes later, you're going to be addressing your subjects on that throne.
